question: From identical restored body states and identical feasible hand joint goals, over one 250 ms hold, with the finger joint servo's per-joint limit (on_per_joint) against the chain's shared factor (on): which rule ends each finger hinge nearer its goal (bend and extend goals, both hands), and does on_per_joint cost overshoot past the goal, shaking (goal crossings, hinge-speed sign changes) or finger_couple tendon force?
sigma_source: measured: root mean square of (latched goal - start angle) over 8 bodies x 44 hinges
verdict_reason: the comparison is complete and every validity check holds
selection_reason: bend: on_per_joint nearer; extend: neither nearer by the line; on_per_joint worse on overshoot_deg, goal_crossings, speed_sign_changes, tendon_largest_limit_force

readings.name: bend goals: body mean of the share of pairs ending nearer the goal under 'on_per_joint' than under 'on'
readings.meaning: 0.5 = the two rules end nearer equally often; 1 = 'on_per_joint' nearer on every pair; 0 = 'on' nearer on every pair (2580 pairs, 8 bodies; pairs within the scatter 0 degrees left out)
readings.baseline: median share of the gap closed in the hold (0 = never moved, 1 = arrived): 'on' 0.382, 'on_per_joint' 0.596; median end residual minus the other rule's, 'on' - 'on_per_joint': 0.588 degrees
readings.statistical_basis: exact two-sided sign-flip count over the body values of (share - 0.5): 2 of 256, line 12

readings.name: extend goals: body mean of the share of pairs ending nearer the goal under 'on_per_joint' than under 'on'
